commit_message:
Bug 1867249, part 1: Implemented new cache to determine selected nodes. r=sefeng,dom-core

Determining if a node is selected is a super-hot code path,
which at times introduces jank both in Reflow and Painting.
This is due to each node comparing its position to the range's start and end point,
which even happens several times (`nsINode::IsSelected()` and `Selection::LookupSelection()`).
In worst cases, this can lead to reflow which takes several minutes.

This patch introduces a cache which contains all fully selected nodes,
and lives throughout one `PresShell::DoReflow()` call.
Collecting all selected nodes of a selection is very fast.
The selected nodes are then stored in a hash set.
During reflow the check if a node is selected first checks the cache
if the node is fully selected, and otherwise goes through the existing
code to check if the node is partially selected.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D217794

fix_commit.message: Bug 1943179 - Add `[[nodiscard]]` to `ContentIterator` methods that return `nsresult`. r=masayuki
fix_commit.author: Jan-Niklas Jaeschke

findings.title: Unchecked return value of iterator initialization leads to use of uninitialized memory
findings.message: The `UnsafePreContentIterator::Init()` method returns an `nsresult` that can indicate failure (e.g., if the range is invalid or collapsed). When the return value is not checked, a failed initialization leaves the iterator's internal pointers (`mCurNode`, `mFirst`, `mLast`, `mClosestCommonInclusiveAncestor`) uninitialized. Subsequently calling `iter.IsDone()` and `iter.Next()` on this uninitialized iterator will dereference garbage or poison pointer values, leading to crashes or potential use-after-free conditions.

related_locations.description: Uninitialized pointer members in ContentIteratorBase class

findings.suggestion: Check the return value of `iter.Init(range)` and skip iteration if it fails. The iterator's internal pointers should also be default-initialized to nullptr to make failed initializations safer.

findings.title: Class members not default-initialized, enabling undefined behavior on failed initialization
findings.message: The `ContentIteratorBase` class declares raw pointer members (`mCurNode`, `mFirst`, `mLast`, `mClosestCommonInclusiveAncestor`) without default initialization. When the `Init()` method fails early (e.g., due to invalid range boundaries), these pointers retain their indeterminate values. Since `IsDone()` checks `!mCurNode` and `GetCurrentNode()` returns `mCurNode`, using an iterator after a failed `Init()` call leads to accessing garbage memory.
findings.suggestion: Default-initialize all pointer members to nullptr. Additionally, add [[nodiscard]] attribute to Init() methods to enforce checking return values at compile time.

ground_truth.root_cause: The root cause is twofold: (1) The `ContentIteratorBase` class did not default-initialize its internal pointer members (`mCurNode`, `mFirst`, `mLast`, `mClosestCommonInclusiveAncestor`), leaving them with indeterminate values when `Init()` fails. (2) The calling code in `SelectionNodeCache::MaybeCollect()` did not check the return value of `iter.Init(range)` before using the iterator, allowing the code to proceed with an improperly initialized iterator.

must_cover.reason: Contains the vulnerable code at lines 348-350 where iter.Init(range) is called without checking the return value. The unchecked nsresult allows the iterator to remain uninitialized if Init() fails, then IsDone() and Next() are called on line 350 with uninitialized pointers (mCurNode, mFirst, mLast, mClosestCommonInclusiveAncestor), causing use of uninitialized memory.

Defines the uninitialized pointer members (mCurNode, mFirst, mLast, mClosestCommonInclusiveAncestor) that remain indeterminate when Init() fails. These members are not default-initialized, making them contain garbage values that are subsequently dereferenced when IsDone() and Next() are called.

Returns nsresult that can indicate failure (e.g., NS_ERROR_FAILURE for collapsed or invalid ranges). When this return value is ignored, the iterator's internal state remains uninitialized, setting up the vulnerability. The Init signature shows it can fail but the caller doesn't check.

Calls MaybeCollect() at line 397-398 which triggers the vulnerable code path. This is the entry point that invokes the caching mechanism where the unchecked iterator initialization occurs, making it part of the vulnerable call chain.
